name: Question 1
problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-2y).$
worked_solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $∇f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-2y)) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡(x-2y) \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-2y)) \\  & =-2{sec}^{2}⁡(x-2y)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡(x-2y)\,i-2{sec}^{2}⁡(x-2y)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find the gradient vector field of the function f(x,y)=tan⁡(x−2y).

a
sec⁡(x−2y)i−2sec⁡(x−2y)j
b
sec2⁡(x−2y)i−sec2⁡(x−2y)j
c
xsec2⁡(x−2y)i−2ysec2⁡(x−2y)j
d
−2sec⁡(x−2y)i+sec⁡(x−2y)j
e
sec2⁡(x−2y)i−2sec2⁡(x−2y)j
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The gradient vector field of a function f is given by ∇f.

First, we find the partial derivatives: fx(x,y)=∂∂x(tan⁡(x−2y))=sec2⁡(x−2y)fy(x,y)=∂∂y(tan⁡(x−2y))=−2sec2⁡(x−2y)

Therefore, the gradient vector field of f(x,y) is ∇f(x,y)=fx(x,y)i+fy(x,y)j=sec2⁡(x−2y)i−2sec2⁡(x−2y)j.
